purpose: Non-standard DSA problems for OA prep — problems that don't map cleanly to a single named pattern (sliding window, two pointers, standard DP, etc). Mix of well-known hard LeetCode problems, real reported OA/interview questions, contest Q3/Q4 problems, and quant-firm style puzzles.

categories.note: No general technique applies — you build small custom logic and validate against many hand-drawn cases (classic 'ad-hoc' USACO framing). Many of the UVa entries below are pulled from a problem set explicitly tagged 'Ad hoc' by competitive programmers.

problems.name: Robot Room Cleaner
problems.description: Control a robot in an unknown grid via only move/turn/clean API calls — no grid is given directly. Explore and clean every reachable cell without getting stuck.
problems.why_nonstandard: Interactive problem — 'DFS' has to be reinvented with virtual coordinate tracking instead of a standard grid traversal.

problems.name: Optiver OA — Balloon Festival
problems.description: A rule-driven simulation of balloons/events over time where you must maintain consistent state across many interacting rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: Reported by candidates as requiring 'systematic modeling + state consistency + boundary sensitivity' rather than a textbook algorithm.

problems.name: Bridge Hand Evaluator
problems.description: Parse a bridge card hand and compute point values / suit distributions per standard bridge scoring rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: Pure rules-encoding problem — the challenge is faithfully implementing a real-world scoring system, not choosing a DS/algorithm.

problems.name: Google Interview — Tile Placement Validator
problems.description: Given an a×b board and m tiles of varying 1×k dimensions, validate whether a placement is legal: axis-aligned, non-overlapping, no touching (even diagonally).
problems.why_nonstandard: The difficulty is inventing the right adjacency/overlap check — no canonical pattern covers 'no corner-touching' constraints.

problems.name: Jolly Jumpers
problems.description: Check whether the absolute differences between consecutive elements of a sequence form a permutation of 1..n-1.
problems.why_nonstandard: Simple to state, but success depends on a quick ad-hoc observation, not a named algorithm.

problems.name: What is the Median?
problems.description: Maintain the running median of a stream of numbers as they arrive.
problems.why_nonstandard: Pre-dates 'two heaps' being a taught pattern — originally an ad-hoc data-structure design exercise.

problems.name: Loansome Car Buyer
problems.description: Simulate monthly car-loan paydown given a payment schedule and early-payment rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: Financial simulation with many small rule interactions — no algorithmic 'trick', just careful state modeling.

problems.name: Request for Proposal
problems.description: Select the cheapest valid combination of vendor bids meeting a set of requirements.
problems.why_nonstandard: Constraint-matching logic that doesn't reduce cleanly to a standard optimization pattern at small scale.

problems.name: Minesweeper
problems.description: Given a minefield, output the number of adjacent mines for every cell.
problems.why_nonstandard: Trivial-looking but a classic ad-hoc grid-neighbor counting exercise with many boundary cases.

problems.name: Contest Scoreboard
problems.description: Compute and rank scoreboard standings for a programming contest given submission logs.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires exactly replicating real scoring/tie-break rules — no DSA pattern, just precise bookkeeping.

problems.name: The Most Potent Corner
problems.description: Determine reachability on a hypercube-like graph of binary strings under specific flip rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: The state space (bit-flip graph) isn't a standard graph model taught in DSA courses.

problems.name: Chessboard in FEN
problems.description: Parse and validate Forsyth–Edwards Notation (FEN) chess position strings.
problems.why_nonstandard: String parsing tied to a real-world domain-specific format, not a generic pattern.

problems.name: Combination Lock
problems.description: Simulate rotating a multi-dial combination lock to reach a target combination with minimum total rotation.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires modeling circular-distance minimization per dial — a small custom insight, not a named technique.

problems.name: What is the Card?
problems.description: Deduce a card's identity from partial dealt-hand information across multiple card games' rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: Domain-specific deduction logic (cards) with no general algorithmic backbone.

problems.name: Rotated square
problems.description: Given the original and a candidate rotated matrix, verify if the candidate is a valid 90°/180°/270° rotation.
problems.why_nonstandard: Coordinate-transform simulation rather than a standard matrix algorithm.

problems.name: Spiral Tap
problems.description: Given a spiral-numbered matrix, find which cell holds a given number (or vice versa).
problems.why_nonstandard: Custom coordinate math for spiral indexing — every spiral problem needs its own derivation.

problems.name: Searching for Nessy
problems.description: Count the minimum number of non-overlapping k×k squares needed to cover all marked cells in a grid.
problems.why_nonstandard: Small ad-hoc covering/counting insight rather than a textbook greedy or DP.

problems.name: Celebrity Jeopardy
problems.description: Reformat Jeopardy-style question/answer text according to specific display rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: Pure output-formatting logic; the 'algorithm' is just correctly following quirky rules.

categories.note: Require modeling continuous or geometric behavior discretely — rare in standard DSA prep, common in quant/trading OAs.

problems.name: Snowflake OA — Mutual Pursuit Points
problems.description: N points each move directly toward the next point cyclically (i chases i+1). Determine whether all points eventually converge to one location.
problems.why_nonstandard: A pursuit-curve geometry problem — convergence only happens when points form a regular polygon (plus collinear edge cases), an insight no DSA pattern teaches.

problems.name: Spiral Matrix III
problems.description: Simulate a spiral walk starting from an arbitrary cell/direction, recording every visited cell (including outside the grid) until all in-bounds cells are covered.
problems.why_nonstandard: Coordinate-geometry simulation with an unusual stopping condition, not DP/graph.

problems.name: Sylvester's Four-Point Problem (coded)
problems.description: Given random points sampled in a region, compute the probability that 4 random points form a convex quadrilateral.
problems.why_nonstandard: Blends combinatorial geometry with probability — no standard template.

problems.name: Erect the Fence
problems.description: Given points representing trees, find the minimum-length fence enclosing all of them (convex hull).
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires implementing a convex-hull algorithm (Graham scan / Andrew's monotone chain) from scratch, including collinear-point edge cases.

problems.name: Max Points on a Line
problems.description: Given 2D points, find the maximum number that lie on the same straight line.
problems.why_nonstandard: Naive slope math breaks on duplicate points and vertical lines — needs careful fraction/gcd-based slope hashing.

problems.name: Rectangle Area II
problems.description: Given a list of axis-aligned rectangles, compute the total area covered by their union.
problems.why_nonstandard: Fuses coordinate compression with a sweep-line — a geometry + data-structure combo rarely drilled together.

problems.name: The Skyline Problem
problems.description: Given building outlines, compute the skyline (max-height silhouette) formed by their union.
problems.why_nonstandard: Classic sweep-line + max-heap fusion; the geometric event-ordering logic is the hard part, not any single DS.

problems.name: Buffon's Needle (coded simulation)
problems.platform: Classical geometric-probability problem, reframed as a coding task
problems.description: Compute or simulate the probability that a randomly dropped needle crosses a line on a floor marked with equally spaced parallel lines.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires translating a continuous-probability derivation into exact/simulated code — a math-heavy reframing with no DSA pattern.

categories.note: Solvable in a few lines once you find the right algebraic reframing — brute force or standard patterns time out.

problems.name: Google Interview — Pairs with a[i] - i = a[j] - j
problems.description: Count/find index pairs (i, j) satisfying a[i] - a[j] = i - j.
problems.why_nonstandard: Collapses once you rearrange to a[i]-i = a[j]-j and bucket by that value — the trick isn't any named pattern.

problems.name: Google Interview — Sort f(x)=ax²+bx+c outputs faster than O(n log n)
problems.description: Given a quadratic function and a sorted input array, produce the sorted output array faster than a generic sort.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires recognizing the parabola's shape and doing a two-pointer merge from the vertex outward.

problems.name: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
problems.description: Flip every element in chosen length-K windows of a binary array so all values become 1, minimizing flip count.
problems.why_nonstandard: Efficient solution needs a difference-array 'lazy flip tracking' trick — greedy-with-a-twist, not textbook greedy.

problems.name: Strange Printer
problems.description: A printer prints only contiguous runs of one character, overwriting existing text; find minimum turns to print a target string.
problems.why_nonstandard: The interval-DP recurrence needs a non-obvious 'merge equal boundary characters' observation.

problems.name: Super Egg Drop
problems.description: Find the minimum number of trials needed to determine the critical floor with K eggs and N floors.
problems.why_nonstandard: The efficient solution flips the DP state to 'how many floors can be resolved with k eggs and m moves' — famously counter-intuitive.

problems.name: Count of Range Sum
problems.description: Count the number of range sums that lie within [lower, upper].
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires combining prefix sums with a merge-sort-based (or BIT-based) counting technique, not a standard sliding window.

problems.name: Russian Doll Envelopes
problems.description: Find the maximum number of envelopes that can be nested inside each other by width and height.
problems.why_nonstandard: The trick — sort by width ascending, height descending, then run LIS on heights — is a single clever reduction most people don't see.

problems.name: Codeforces 1372E — Omkar and Last Floor
problems.description: A DP problem cited by a CF round coordinator as an example of a 'DP' problem appearing alongside heavily ad-hoc/constructive rounds.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires an unusual state reformulation before standard DP techniques apply.

problems.name: Codeforces 1363F — Rotating Substrings
problems.description: An edit-distance-style DP problem with a rotation twist, also cited by a CF coordinator as a DP example.
problems.why_nonstandard: Combines string-rotation reasoning with a DP recurrence not found in standard edit-distance drilling.

problems.name: Smallest Good Base
problems.description: Find the smallest base k such that a given number n can be represented as all 1's in base k.
problems.why_nonstandard: Needs binary search combined with geometric-series algebra to bound the digit count — a pure math derivation.

problems.name: K-th Smallest in Multiplication Table
problems.description: Find the k-th smallest number in an m×n multiplication table.
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved via binary search on the answer value with a counting function — not a direct search/sort problem despite appearances.

problems.name: Find the Closest Palindrome
problems.description: Given a numeric string, find the closest different palindrome number.
problems.why_nonstandard: Correctness hinges on generating the right small set of palindrome candidates (mirroring, ±1 on the prefix, all-9s, all-0s-plus-one) — an insight problem full of edge cases.

problems.name: Distinct Subsequences II
problems.description: Count the number of distinct non-empty subsequences of a string.
problems.why_nonstandard: The counting DP needs a 'subtract the last time this character was seen' dedup trick that isn't part of standard subsequence-counting drills.

categories.category: Contest Q3/Q4 Problems Needing Rare Techniques
categories.note: The last problem(s) of LeetCode weekly/biweekly contests and Codeforces/AtCoder hardest slots often combine two patterns or need an uncommon trick.

problems.name: Weekly Contest 397 Q4 — Find Permutation minimizing score with lexicographic tie-break
problems.description: Given adjacency constraints on a permutation of size up to ~14, find the arrangement minimizing a defined 'score', outputting the lexicographically smallest optimum.
problems.why_nonstandard: Small n hints at bitmask DP, but naive O(n!) backtracking 'appears' to pass weak tests; the lexicographic tie-break is what actually separates correct bitmask-DP from lucky brute force.

problems.name: Cat and Mouse
problems.description: Two players move on a graph with different rules (Mouse can enter a 'hole' node, Cat cannot); determine the outcome with optimal play.
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved via retrograde/topological game-state analysis, working backward from known terminal states — rarely taught alongside standard graph/DP.

problems.name: Bricks Falling When Hit
problems.description: Simulate bricks falling after a sequence of removals in a grid; report how many bricks fall after each removal.
problems.why_nonstandard: The efficient trick is processing removals in reverse and *adding* bricks back with Union-Find — offline-reverse-processing, not part of typical pattern training.

problems.name: Codeforces-style Div1 D/E — Interactive + Constructive combo
problems.description: Problems requiring both interaction with an adaptive judge and construction of a valid output under combinatorial constraints.
problems.why_nonstandard: 'Interactive' and 'constructive' are their own Codeforces tags precisely because they need custom, problem-specific reasoning instead of a known algorithm.

problems.name: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps
problems.description: Count the number of ways a pointer can return to position 0 after exactly steps moves within bounds.
problems.why_nonstandard: A bounded-random-walk DP that needs a non-obvious pruning bound (steps//2) to stay within limits.

problems.name: Parallel Courses III
problems.description: Given course prerequisites and per-course completion times, find the minimum time to complete all courses.
problems.why_nonstandard: Fuses topological sort with a 'longest path/critical path' DP — a combination not covered by either pattern alone.

problems.name: Minimize Malware Spread II
problems.description: Determine which single node to remove from a graph to minimize the eventual malware-infected node count.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires careful union-find bookkeeping to isolate each initially-infected node's unique 'reach' — subtle counting, easy to get wrong.

problems.name: Swim in Rising Water
problems.description: Find the minimum time such that a path exists from top-left to bottom-right of a grid, given cell elevations and rising water level.
problems.why_nonstandard: A binary-search-on-answer + BFS/Union-Find hybrid — neither technique alone is sufficient.

problems.name: Race Car
problems.description: A car can accelerate or reverse; find minimum instructions to reach a target position.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires BFS over an abstract (position, speed) state space with jump-ahead heuristics — an unusual state modeling exercise.

problems.name: Stamping the Sequence
problems.description: Determine an order of stamp placements that builds a target string from all '?' characters.
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved by simulating in reverse — repeatedly 'un-stamping' matches — a greedy-simulation idea with no standard name.

problems.name: Cherry Pickup
problems.description: Two paths traverse a grid simultaneously (from two agents) to collect maximum cherries without conflicting.
problems.why_nonstandard: The state design — modeling two simultaneous single-agent paths as one combined DP state — is a famously non-obvious reduction.

problems.name: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
problems.description: Find the shortest path in an undirected graph that visits every node, revisits and edges allowed.
problems.why_nonstandard: Fuses BFS with bitmask state tracking — effectively a small TSP layered on top of graph BFS.

problems.name: Cat and Mouse II
problems.description: A grid variant of Cat and Mouse with walls, jump distances, and food, determining the game outcome under optimal play.
problems.why_nonstandard: An even larger retrograde game-state space than the graph version, with extra movement rules to encode correctly.

problems.name: Word Break II
problems.description: Return all possible sentences formed by segmenting a string into dictionary words.
problems.why_nonstandard: Naive backtracking with memoization has a subtle trap: memoizing the wrong thing (booleans instead of sentence lists) blows up exponentially.

problems.name: AtCoder Grand Contest 'Ex'-style problem
problems.description: The final problem of an AtCoder Grand Contest, typically requiring a novel combinatorial or structural insight unique to that problem.
problems.why_nonstandard: By design, AGC 'Ex' problems avoid reusing known patterns — each one needs its own from-scratch insight.

categories.category: Puzzle-Style Problems (Quant Firms: Jane Street, Optiver, Akuna, DE Shaw, Citadel)
categories.note: Often math/logic puzzles reframed as coding tasks — no DSA pattern covers them by design.

problems.name: Jane Street Monthly Puzzle — Subtiles 2
problems.description: Fill a grid with positive integers so each value k forms a connected 'k-omino' that must fully contain the shape formed by all (k-1)-cells, with some cells pre-labeled using obscured variables.
problems.why_nonstandard: A constraint-satisfaction/construction puzzle over polyominoes — closer to combinatorial search + geometric reasoning than any interview DSA pattern.

problems.name: Jane Street — Robot Capture the Flag (archived puzzle)
problems.description: A pursuit/game-theory puzzle involving robots capturing a flag under movement rules, requiring optimal-strategy reasoning.
problems.why_nonstandard: Game-theoretic puzzle with continuous or semi-continuous state space — not a standard discrete game-DP problem.

problems.name: Akuna-style OA — Two-Heap Order Book Simulation
problems.description: Maintain a live order book (buy/sell) with running median/VWAP/PnL using two heaps and prefix sums, under streaming updates.
problems.why_nonstandard: A composite 'systems micro-simulation' combining heaps, streaming windows, and financial domain logic rather than one isolated pattern.

problems.name: Quant-firm probability-simulation archetype (DE Shaw / Citadel style)
problems.platform: Common OA archetype at quant firms
problems.description: Code an exact or Monte-Carlo estimate of a probability defined by a multi-step random process (e.g., expected number of trials until a stopping condition).
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires translating a probability-theory derivation into precise code rather than applying a named DSA pattern; this is a reported category rather than one fixed problem.

problems.name: HackerRank / Project Euler-style number puzzle
problems.description: A self-contained numeric puzzle (e.g., sums over divisor functions, digit properties, or recurrence-based counting) similar in style to Project Euler problems.
problems.why_nonstandard: These lean on number-theory insight and efficient computation of a closed form, rather than a taught DSA pattern.

categories.category: Design / Data-Structure Problems With No Standard Blueprint
categories.note: You must invent a custom data structure combo; there's no single 'named' structure that solves it directly.

problems.name: Design In-Memory File System
problems.description: Implement a file system supporting path creation, file writing/reading, and directory listing, entirely in-memory.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires a custom trie-like tree with mixed file/directory node types — no single textbook DS matches the requirement set.

problems.name: LFU Cache
problems.description: Design a cache evicting the Least Frequently Used item (recency as tie-break) with O(1) get/put.
problems.why_nonstandard: Needs hashmap + frequency-bucketed doubly linked lists — a structure invented specifically for this problem.

problems.name: Design Skiplist
problems.description: Implement a skip list supporting search/add/erase with expected O(log n) operations via probabilistic balancing.
problems.why_nonstandard: Skip lists are rarely taught as a core DSA topic, so most candidates are building the structure's logic from first principles.

problems.name: Maximum Frequency Stack
problems.description: Design a stack-like structure where pop() removes the most frequent element, breaking ties by most-recently-pushed.
problems.why_nonstandard: Needs a frequency-bucketed stack-of-stacks design with no standard name.

problems.name: All O`one Data Structure
problems.description: Design a structure supporting increment/decrement of string keys and O(1) retrieval of the max- and min-count keys.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires a doubly linked list of count-buckets, each holding a set of keys — a bespoke combination.

problems.name: Design Twitter
problems.description: Design a simplified Twitter supporting posting tweets, following/unfollowing, and retrieving a user's most recent feed.
problems.why_nonstandard: Fuses a heap-based k-way merge with a follow-graph — a systems-design flavored problem, not a single pattern.

problems.name: Data Stream as Disjoint Intervals
problems.description: Given numbers arriving one at a time, maintain the list of disjoint intervals covering all numbers seen so far.
problems.why_nonstandard: Needs online interval merge/split logic, typically via an ordered map — not the offline interval-merge pattern most people practice.

problems.name: Random Pick with Weight
problems.description: Design a structure to randomly pick an index proportional to given weights.
problems.why_nonstandard: Combines prefix sums with binary search purely to support weighted random sampling — an unusual use of both techniques together.

problems.name: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
problems.description: Design a structure supporting O(1) insert, remove, and get-random, allowing duplicate values.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires an array + hashmap-of-index-sets combo with careful swap-to-delete logic to keep true O(1) with duplicates.

categories.note: Graph problems that need an unusual remodeling of the input before any standard graph algorithm applies.

problems.name: Number of Islands II
problems.description: Land cells are added to a grid one at a time; report the number of islands after each addition.
problems.why_nonstandard: An 'online' union-find problem — most island-counting practice is offline/batch, so incremental merging needs its own logic.

problems.name: Making A Large Island
problems.description: Flip exactly one 0 to 1 to maximize the resulting island's size.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires precomputing component sizes and IDs, then checking merges at each candidate flip — a two-pass design beyond plain flood fill.

problems.name: Path With Maximum Minimum Value
problems.description: Find a path from top-left to bottom-right maximizing the minimum cell value along the path.
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved via binary search + BFS, or a Prim's-like max-heap traversal — neither is the 'obvious' first approach.

problems.name: Bus Routes
problems.description: Given bus routes as sets of stops, find the minimum number of buses to get from a source stop to a target stop.
problems.why_nonstandard: The BFS graph must be built over *routes*, not stops — an unintuitive remodeling before BFS applies.

problems.name: Reconstruct Itinerary
problems.description: Reconstruct an itinerary using every ticket exactly once, in lexical order when multiple valid itineraries exist.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires Hierholzer's algorithm for Eulerian paths — a technique almost never covered in standard graph-pattern prep.

problems.name: Alien Dictionary
problems.description: Given a list of words sorted according to an unknown alien alphabet's rules, derive a valid character ordering.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires building a graph from implicit pairwise word comparisons before topological sort applies — the graph isn't given, it must be derived.

problems.name: Critical Connections in a Network
problems.description: Find all bridges (critical edges) in a connected undirected graph.
problems.why_nonstandard: Needs Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm with discovery/low-link times — a rarely-drilled graph technique.

problems.name: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
problems.description: Each grid cell has a fixed direction; find the minimum number of cells to redirect to create a valid path from start to end.
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved via 0-1 BFS (deque-based), a technique that blends BFS and Dijkstra but is taught in neither standard track.

problems.name: Word Ladder II
problems.description: Find all shortest transformation sequences from a start word to an end word, changing one letter at a time via a dictionary.
problems.why_nonstandard: Efficient solutions need BFS layering plus careful backward path reconstruction to avoid exponential blowup — notoriously easy to TLE.

problems.name: Cracking the Safe
problems.description: Construct the shortest possible string that contains every possible password of given length and alphabet size as a substring.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires constructing a De Bruijn sequence via Hierholzer's algorithm on an implicit graph — a construction problem in disguise.

problems.name: Number of Distinct Islands II
problems.description: Count islands that are distinct under rotation and reflection.
problems.why_nonstandard: Needs canonicalizing each island's shape across up to 8 geometric transforms — geometry fused into what looks like a pure graph problem.

problems.name: Employee Free Time
problems.description: Given each employee's busy time intervals, find the common free time slots across all employees.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires merging intervals across multiple independent lists simultaneously — a multi-list interval-merge variant beyond the standard single-list version.

categories.note: The algorithm is often simple; the difficulty is in correctly handling a large space of edge cases in a formal grammar or format.

problems.name: Text Justification
problems.description: Format a list of words into justified lines of exact width, following specific left/full-justification spacing rules.
problems.why_nonstandard: No algorithm to speak of — the challenge is exactly replicating a formatting spec with many off-by-one traps.

problems.name: Number of Atoms
problems.description: Parse a chemical formula string (with nested parentheses and multipliers) into a count of each atom.
problems.why_nonstandard: A small recursive-descent parser is needed — grammar parsing, not a DSA pattern.

problems.name: Basic Calculator III
problems.description: Evaluate a string expression with +, -, *, /, and nested parentheses without using library eval.
problems.why_nonstandard: Effectively building a small expression parser/evaluator with operator precedence — a compiler-adjacent task.

problems.name: Basic Calculator IV
problems.description: Evaluate an expression containing variables and return the result as a simplified, sorted polynomial.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires symbolic polynomial representation and combination — well beyond simple arithmetic parsing.

problems.name: Valid Number
problems.description: Determine whether a string represents a valid number, accounting for signs, decimals, and exponents.
problems.why_nonstandard: Notorious for its sheer number of edge cases; the difficulty is exhaustive case coverage, not algorithm design.

problems.name: Regular Expression Matching
problems.description: Implement regex matching supporting '.' and '*'.
problems.why_nonstandard: The DP recurrence for '*' (zero-or-more of the preceding element) is a genuinely tricky recursive case most people get wrong on the first try.

problems.name: Wildcard Matching
problems.description: Implement wildcard pattern matching supporting '?' and '*'.
problems.why_nonstandard: Similar DP subtlety to regex matching, but with different semantics for '*' — easy to conflate the two and get wrong.

problems.name: Count Different Palindromic Subsequences
problems.description: Count the number of distinct non-empty palindromic subsequences of a string, modulo 1e9+7.
problems.why_nonstandard: The interval-DP recurrence requires careful case-splitting on matching boundary characters to avoid double-counting.

problems.name: Palindrome Pairs
problems.description: Given a list of words, find all pairs of indices (i, j) such that concatenating words[i] and words[j] forms a palindrome.
problems.why_nonstandard: Efficient solutions need a trie or hashmap keyed on reversed prefixes/suffixes — a non-obvious reformation of a brute-force check.

problems.name: Concatenated Words
problems.description: Find all words in a list that can be formed by concatenating other words from the same list.
problems.why_nonstandard: A DP-over-string-segmentation problem layered on top of a word-break check — the composition of two ideas is what makes it hard.

problems.name: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.description: Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings into one string and decode it back, robust to any characters within the strings.
problems.why_nonstandard: A classic 'systems' interview question about designing a delimiter-safe protocol — not a DSA pattern at all.

problems.name: Freedom Trail
problems.description: Find the minimum number of steps to spell a target word by rotating a ring and pressing a button to select letters.
problems.why_nonstandard: The DP state (ring position, target index) is easy to define but the transition requires careful handling of multiple ring positions per letter.

categories.note: Problems where a closed-form or counting insight replaces brute enumeration, often needed when n is astronomically large.

problems.name: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
problems.description: Count all numbers with unique digits in the range [0, 10^n).
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved with a direct combinatorial counting formula rather than enumeration — most people default to brute force first.

problems.name: Numbers With Repeated Digits
problems.description: Count how many numbers in [1, n] have at least one repeated digit.
problems.why_nonstandard: Solved via digit DP on the complement (numbers with all-unique digits), a technique rarely covered outside competitive programming.

problems.name: Ugly Number III
problems.description: Find the n-th number divisible by a, b, or c.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires inclusion-exclusion with LCMs combined with binary search on the answer value.

problems.name: Nth Magical Number
problems.description: Find the n-th positive number divisible by a or b.
problems.why_nonstandard: Same inclusion-exclusion + binary-search combo as Ugly Number III, but with modular-arithmetic answer requirements.

problems.name: Minimum Number of Days to Eat N Oranges
problems.description: Given rules to eat 1, half, or a third of remaining oranges per day, find the minimum days to eat all n oranges (n up to 2*10^9).
problems.why_nonstandard: n is too large for direct DP — requires memoized recursion that exploits the halving/thirding branching factor to stay small.

problems.name: Super Pow
problems.description: Compute a^b mod 1337, where b is given as an array of digits (potentially huge).
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires decomposing modular exponentiation digit-by-digit using properties of modular arithmetic, not standard fast-pow.

problems.name: Project Euler-style Divisor/Sigma Sum Puzzle
problems.description: Compute a closed-form or efficiently-summed quantity over divisors or digit properties of numbers up to a very large bound.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires number-theoretic identities (e.g., sieve-based divisor sums) rather than direct computation, since brute force is infeasible at the given bound.

problems.name: Broken Stick Triangle Probability (coded exactly)
problems.platform: Classical combinatorics/geometric-probability problem, reframed as a coding task
problems.description: If a line segment is broken randomly into three pieces, compute the exact probability that they form a triangle.
problems.why_nonstandard: Requires translating a geometric-probability proof into exact fractional computation rather than applying any DSA pattern.

how_to_use_this_list: Don't look for a pattern first — draw 3-4 small examples by hand before writing any code, per the classic USACO ad-hoc approach.
For each problem, write down what makes it break the 'usual' approach (brute force too slow? hidden edge case? needs a reframing?) before attempting the fix.
Time-box these to 40-60 minutes each — the goal is exposure to reasoning-under-ambiguity, not pattern drilling.
For quant/trading firm OAs specifically, prioritize the Geometry, Puzzle-Style, and Number-Theory categories — these firms weight modeling ability over raw algorithm speed.
For big-tech OAs (Amazon/Google/Meta), the Graph & Union-Find Curveballs and Contest Q3/Q4 categories are the closest match to what's actually reported.
